predicate_note: Biolink 4.2.5 has no dedicated 'is metabolized by' predicate, and KG2c stores no has_input/has_metabolite/physically_interacts_with edges between codeine and any gene. The Biolink-canonical form for 'enzyme X metabolizes drug Y' is X affects Y with qualifiers; KG2c has exactly one such edge (NCBIGene:1565 CYP2D6 -> codeine, infores:ncit, original predicate NCIT:enzyme_metabolizes_chemical_or_drug), but KG2 remapped it with object_aspect_qualifier 'localization' (apparent remap artifact), and that direction returns only 1 result. Gold therefore uses the drug-subject direction codeine -> biolink:affects -> Gene, which returns 8 genes: 3 metabolizing enzymes (the gold answers) plus 5 distractors (opioid receptors OPRM1/OPRD1/OPRK1, transporter ABCB1, androgen receptor AR). The question tests whether the system filters the result set down to enzymes.

validation.predicate_fix: No 'metabolized by' predicate in Biolink 4.2.5 / KG2c; gold uses biolink:affects (codeine as subject). See predicate_note.

verification_guide.summary: 3 enzymes covering both metabolic phases and all three named routes of codeine metabolism in the FDA label: CYP2D6 (O-demethylation to morphine, bioactivation), CYP3A4 (N-demethylation to norcodeine), UGT2B7 (glucuronidation to codeine-6-glucuronide). All three are verified against the FDA codeine sulfate label (DailyMed, section 12.3) and CYP2D6 additionally against the CPIC opioid guideline. All three are returned by PloverDB for the gold query.
sources_used: DailyMed FDA-approved drug label, CODEINE SULFATE tablet (Hikma), section 12.3 Pharmacokinetics -> Metabolism: all 3 answers
PubMed abstract of the 2021 CPIC guideline for CYP2D6, OPRM1 and COMT genotypes and select opioid therapy (PMID 33387367): CYP2D6
verification_guide.how_to_verify_a_dailymed_entry: On the DailyMed CODEINE SULFATE tablet page (Hikma; label revised 12/2025, SPL version 25), open the FULL PRESCRIBING INFORMATION section "12 CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY" -> "12.3 Pharmacokinetics" (expand it if collapsed). Under the run-in heading "Metabolism:" the first sentence gives the 70-80% / 5-10% / ~10% split; the second sentence names the UGT enzymes and the third sentence names CYP2D6 and CYP3A4.
verification_guide.how_to_verify_a_pubmed_entry: Open the PubMed URL; the quoted sentence is the second sentence of the Abstract block. (Scripted fetches of pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov hit a bot check, so the curator verified the abstract text through NCBI E-utilities efetch, db=pubmed, id=33387367, which returns the same abstract.)
verification_guide.cross_check_with_ploverdb: Each verified_answer CURIE was confirmed present in the PloverDB result set for the gold query (n0=CHEBI:16714, n1=biolink:Gene, e0: n0 -biolink:affects-> n1) on 2026-09-28. PloverDB returned 8 gene CURIEs; the 3 enzymes are the gold subset, the other 5 are non-enzyme distractors.
verification_guide.intentionally_omitted: UGT2B4 (NCBIGene:7363) is named by the FDA label as a major C6G-forming enzyme, but it is reachable only through the HMDB related_to edges, not through biolink:affects, so it fails the 'present in the gold-query result set' rule. CYP2C9 and CYP2C19 (picked by pilot t03 from the related_to set) are HMDB protein associations that the FDA label does not name as codeine-metabolizing enzymes; not gold. OPRM1/OPRD1/OPRK1 (receptor targets, DrugBank/DrugCentral agonist edges), ABCB1 (efflux transporter) and AR (DGIdb edge with no interaction type) are in the result set but are not enzymes that metabolize codeine.

curation_notes: The KG edges that put the 3 enzymes in the result set are DGIdb 'affects' edges at knowledge_level=prediction with no interaction type. They assert an unspecified drug-gene interaction, not 'metabolized by'. The enzyme role comes from the external evidence, not from the KG edge; a faithful answer should say so.

Scoring caveat: the scorer's predicate_match is exact list equality. Pilot t03 used biolink:related_to (answer category Protein), which would score as a predicate mismatch under this gold even though its picks overlapped the gold answers. If you consider related_to acceptable for metabolism questions (it holds the HMDB enzyme associations and UGT2B4), change the gold predicate; the gold answers are present in both result sets.
Only 3 answers meet both rules (in the result set, and named by an authoritative source). This is below the 5 used in q1 but within the 3-5 target.
